Figure 1:LIBERO-Industry overview.Motivated by industrial process constraints,
the benchmark evaluates generalist robot policies across three classic industrial scenarios.

Figure 2:Task generation and scripted demonstration collection inLIBERO-Industry.BDDL specifies objects, process states, and goals; sampled layouts pass a feasibility gate or are resampled (top).
A task-specific scripted expert attempts a rollout from a fixed initial state and seed (bottom).
The diagram shows completion, kinematic-safety, and replay checks before accepted trajectories are stored as HDF5 demonstrations with provenance.
Failed attempts can prompt replay-guided collector refinement.

Figure 3:Cumulative diagnostic stress progression forπ0.5\pi_{0.5}.Each bar denotes complete-task success of the stress settings for n trials (D0–D1:n=200n=200; D2–D6:n=240n=240), andPCRT\mathrm{PCR}_{\mathrm{T}}denotes mean target-object transfer completion. Stars show mean policy steps over successful trajectories; D6 has no successful trajectories.
The progression is diagnostic rather than causal.

Figure 4:Real-world validation.A:AUBOi5H–CTAG2F90D D2S workcell.B:Per-step release-on-tray success forS1andS2at conveyor speeds of 0.03 and 0.05 m/s over 24 trials per condition; the table reports aggregate target-transfer completion asPCRT\mathrm{PCR}_{\mathrm{T}}out of 72 planned placements.C:Target-transfer completion (PCRT\mathrm{PCR}_{\mathrm{T}}) under five physical operating-condition variations, with exact values labeled.

header: Appendix CEvaluation Protocol and Extended Results

images.caption:
Figure 8:Trajectory-level failure classification.Each episode is evaluated along the reach–grasp–lift–transport–place sequence.
The decision rules expose the operational thresholds used for stage-specific labels, while workspace violations, joint-limit saturation, and unmatched cases remain global or fallback outcomes.

Figure 9:Representative failure trajectories.Each row shows three temporally ordered frames from one failed rollout, followed by the trajectory-level classifier output and its frequency within the corresponding diagnostic stage.
The examples link the aggregate categories in Figure3to observable trajectory behavior and are illustrative rather than exhaustive.
